traits.habitat_notes: Native to eastern and central North America: disturbed ground, pastures, clearings, thickets, woodland borders and roadsides, 0-1400 m; naturalised in Europe and Asia.
traits.habit_notes: Dies back each winter to a thick, white, fleshy taproot; one to several stout stems from the crown, green turning red or purple late in the season, pith chambered. Upright early in the season, spreading and leaning later under the weight of fruit. Racemes stand opposite the leaves and droop; berries ripen from green through red to purple-black on pink stalks, flowers and fruit together on one raceme.
